# `Csv`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Csv — CSV encode + decode.

Operates on whole-CSV documents in memory via the `Csv` record:
a `List String` header and a `List (List String)` body.  The
streaming reader (`parseStreamFromFile`) handles large files
without materialising the whole document.

Delimiter handling: `parse` / `encode` use ',' by default.  Use
`parseWithDelimiter` / `encodeWithDelimiter` for ';', '\\t', etc.

## `Csv`

A parsed CSV document.

  * `header` — the first row of the document, treated as the
    column names.
  * `rows` — every subsequent row.  Each row is a `List String`
    of cell values in column order.

This is a record alias so callers can construct it directly to
feed into `encode`.

## `defaultCsv`

```ipe
defaultCsv : Csv
```

`defaultCsv` — empty CSV document (no header, no rows).  Builder
chain stays source-compat when v0.17+ adds optional fields.

## `withHeader`

```ipe
withHeader : List String -> Csv -> Csv
```

`withHeader ["id", "email"] csv` — replace the header row.

## `withRows`

```ipe
withRows : List (List String) -> Csv -> Csv
```

`withRows [["1", "a@example.com"], ["2", "b@example.com"]] csv`
— replace the body rows.

## `parse`

```ipe
parse : String -> Result Error Csv
```

`parse text` — parse `text` as comma-delimited CSV.  The first
row is treated as the header.  Returns `Err Error` on
malformed input.

## `parseWithDelimiter`

```ipe
parseWithDelimiter : String -> String -> Result Error Csv
```

`parseWithDelimiter delim text` — like `parse` but with a
custom single-character delimiter.

## `encode`

```ipe
encode : Csv -> String
```

`encode csv` — encode `csv` back to a comma-delimited string.
Cells containing the delimiter, double quotes, or newlines are
quoted per RFC 4180.

## `encodeWithDelimiter`

```ipe
encodeWithDelimiter : String -> Csv -> String
```

`encodeWithDelimiter delim csv` — like `encode` but with a
custom delimiter.

## `parseStreamFromFile`

```ipe
parseStreamFromFile : Path -> Task Error (List (List String))
```

`parseStreamFromFile path` — stream-read a CSV file at the
validated `path` into memory as `List (List String)` (including
the header).  The `Path` argument enforces NUL-byte and
`..`-traversal guards at the type level.  Uses a buffered reader
so it doesn't materialise the raw file before parsing, making it
suitable for large exports.  For files >1 GB, prefer a worker
`Task` that chunks by row count.  Use `Path.fromString` to
construct the `Path` argument.
